rules: Figma is the visual source of truth. Every template links to its Figma frames. Those designs are meant to be built as designed, not reinterpreted. Fonts, colors, sizes and positions come from Figma. If something in Figma can't be built or looks inconsistent, raise it, don't silently change it.

This spec is for auto-generation first and manual creation (Flow 3) second. Every ready-for-dev template now has a final manual-creation contract; see the Manual creation section of each template and the shared manual creation rules.
Only build templates marked ready-for-dev. Other statuses are shown for context and planning.

Never invent data. When a field is missing, follow the template's fallback rules. If a fallback isn't defined, the template isn't eligible for auto-generation in that case. This follows Core Engine FR-1: missing values are explicit unknowns, never guessed.

Every text field declares its source. Each one is either generated by AI (and at which engine stage), filled by software from existing data, or static. This matches the template catalog that Core Engine Stage 3 expects (Core Engine PRD 4.8, 5.5 and prompt 9.8).

AI text constraints are guidance, not hard limits. Character limits are written into the AI prompts so the output fits naturally. The software limits (shrinking text, trimming) are only a safety net for extreme cases.
templates.json wins. If the website and the JSON ever disagree, the JSON is correct. Every change bumps the version and adds a changelog line.
Writing style for all visible text: plain and direct. Don't use the — or -- characters; use commas or parentheses instead.
readyForDevChecklist: Figma section named with the tracker number; frames and layers use clear names (photo_slot, line_1, message...)
Output sizes confirmed for both 2:3 and 9:16; unused frames removed
Text blocks built with auto-layout or fixed text boxes, so they adapt to the length of the text
Every field has a source, constraints and a fallback
No open blockers (asset swaps that don't change the layout can be followUps)

Match orientation to the slot, else cover-crop from the center.
Single-photo templates: the group cover (5.4) when its orientation fits.
formattingRules: Place names: English (Lisbon, not Lisboa), the nearest city as stored by the place lookup (4.1). No finer detail.
Dates use the photo's local capture date. Each template sets its own format.
Missing values are never shown as "unknown" or as an empty label. Follow the template's fallback, or the template isn't eligible.
Temperature: whole degrees, °C by default, °F when the device region is the US (lookup.temperature_unit).
Altitude: whole metres, rounded to the nearest 10m at 100m and above.

Barcodes are decorative and fixed: the barcodes in #20 (part of the ticket art) and #18 (a fixed vector pattern) encode nothing, link nowhere and never change per postcard. (#30 and #32 no longer have one.)

QR code (#18, #19, #20, #30, #34): one fixed vector, qr_code.svg, that opens https://www.awefullpeople.com/journeyonwardapp. It's the same on every postcard and is never generated per postcard. The link may change later; that means swapping the SVG asset.

Multi-photo templates: every photo comes from one group (Stage 2 members), unless the template says otherwise. With fewer distinct photos than the template's minimum, it isn't eligible for that group.
renderingRules: Fonts: each text field names the real font (Regina's design) and a dev stand-in (a Google Font). Build with the stand-in now. The real font files are being licensed and will be swapped in later (a follow-up on each template, not a blocker). Where a real font can't be licensed, a replacement will be chosen.

Overlay layers: some templates put a fixed texture or glow layer over the photo with a blend mode. Render it with the blend mode given (React Native Skia supports Soft Light and Hard Light). Full frame 1080x1620, transparent where empty. Only if blend modes can't be done in the renderer: draw the overlay at normal blend and 35% opacity, and flag it so the visual can be checked.
Text colors are fixed per template for now. A contrast-based variant (Stage 1b suggesting colors) may come later.

Shrink rule (text): render at max size; if wider than the safe width, shrink down to the min size. If it still doesn't fit, follow the field's fallback, or the template isn't eligible for that photo in auto mode.
All positions are 1x pixels in the 2:3 frame (1080x1620). Every template also has a 9:16 frame (1080x1920).
manualCreationRules: Entry: the user opens a photo (or a group) and picks a template from the gallery. Every template is offered, including ones that aren't eligible in auto mode; missing data simply leaves those fields empty for the user to fill.

Photos: single-photo templates use the open photo. Multi-photo templates are prefilled with the auto picks from that photo's group (3.2); the user can tap any slot to swap in any photo from the trip (not only the group). Export stays disabled until every slot has a photo; empty slots show "Add photo".

Text: every text field is prefilled with its auto value (same source and fallbacks as auto mode) and is editable. Static text (labels, brand lines) is not editable. Clearing a field hides it and the layout follows that field's fallback case.
Limits: each editable field has a hard character cap, the length that still fits its safe width at the minimum size. The shrink rule (3.4) applies while typing.
AI text: manual mode never calls the AI. If an AI field has no value (photo not analyzed yet), it starts empty with a placeholder hint taken from the field's example.
Data fields (dates, places, weather, altitude, codes) are edited as plain text; no validation beyond the character cap. Date fields keep the template's format as a placeholder.
Variants: when a template has variants, the user can switch between them; for #9 the variant follows how many photos the user adds (5 to 7).
Fixed: layout, positions, rotation, fonts and colors can't be changed (except where a variant changes them). No dragging or resizing in the MVP.
Size: the user chooses 2:3 or 9:16 when exporting; both are always available.
Set rules don't apply: maxPerOutputSet, the caption-sticker limit and "#7 and #32 not together" only apply to auto-generated sets.
priorityNote: These priorities, and the overall logic for which postcards are shown to the user, are a first version. They will be tuned after the first production build, based on real results. They may also change once the voice and tone guide exists, which will in turn change Stage 3 of the Core Engine (PR-5 template matching and template text). Build them as configuration (one table, easy to change), not hard-coded logic.

fields.label: Line 1
fields.constraints: One word, ideally 5-12 characters. If the leading word is under 5 characters, use it plus the next word, as long as together they stay within 12.
fields.aiGuidance: sticker_text: a short caption of what the photo shows, split across two lines of a sticker. line_1: the leading word of the caption, ideally 5 to 12 letters (for example "Outdoor"). If the most natural leading word is shorter than 5 letters, you may use two words, as long as together they stay within 12 letters. Together, line_1 + line_2 must read as one natural phrase. Aim for the sweet spot between sounding natural and fitting these lengths. Treat the lengths as targets, not hard rules. Describe only what is visible. No feelings, no identities or relationships, and no place names (the place is added separately). Follows Core Engine Section 8 guardrails.
fields.safetyNet: Software shrink: render at max size, reduce down to min size if too wide. Below min size: if two words, keep only the first word; a single word may go below minimum.

fields.label: Line 2
fields.constraints: Continues line 1 as one natural phrase. About 20 characters.
fields.aiGuidance: line_2: the rest of the caption, about 20 characters or fewer (for example "summer festival"). Treat the length as a target, not a hard rule.
fields.safetyNet: Software shrink down to min size. Below min size: wrap onto a second line. Never rewrite or cut words.

fields.label: Line 3
fields.constraints: The city name (about 20 characters); shrinks to fit.
fields.safetyNet: Software shrink down to min size. Below min size: use the country instead (or "in {country}" in the place-only case).
fields.fallback: Country, see fallback cases for the rest.

rendering: Color: fixed yellow #F2C305 on all three lines for the MVP.
Shadow: on the whole text block, drop shadow, black 35%, offset x 0 y 2, blur 12, spread 0.
Layout: the three lines stack with 0 spacing, left aligned. The block sits 48px from the left edge and is vertically centered in the frame. Line 3 is indented 84px.

Below min size (extreme cases only): line_1 drops to one word if two words still don't fit (a single word may go below minimum); line_2 wraps onto a second line, never rewritten or cut; line_3 uses the country instead.

photos.crop: Photo 1 (window): cover-cropped into the stamp mask. Photo 2 (bottom): cover crop.
photos.groupSelection: Same picking rule as #24: 2 different photos from one group, photo 1 the better-ranked/close subject, photo 2 the next-ranked/wider scene.

autoGeneration.eligibleWhen: 2 distinct photos exist in the group and a place exists.
autoGeneration.priority: Medium: needs 2 distinct photos from one group plus data (Needs AI text or data that is often missing (landmark, weather, altitude, season), or 2 to 3 photos from one group.)

fallbackCases.then: country used in title and place_name

rendering: trip_title centered x540, y146, safe width 920.
label left edge x605, center y319.
place_name left edge x604, center y382, safe width 420.
date left edge x603, center y467.
weather left edge x608, center y523.
altitude left edge x604, center y608, safe width 420.

9:16 derivation rule: the 2:3 design is centered in the taller frame (every layer moves down 150px), except background layers (photos, preset backgrounds, overlays, tints, colored headers, paper blocks): touching both top and bottom edge in 2:3 stays at the top and grows 300px taller (full bleed, cover crop, never stretched); touching only the top edge stays at the top and grows 150px; touching only the bottom edge moves down 150px and grows 150px. Photos keep their cover crop, nothing is stretched. Full-frame overlay PNGs are drawn cover-scaled to 1080x1920 when they cover the whole 2:3 frame, else moved down 150px. Page templates (#30, #32, #34) use their own page_margin_9x16.png. In 9:16, all text keeps the same size, safe width and fallback as in 2:3.

notes: 2 photos (window and bottom must be different photos); text block editable.

followUps: Swap stand-in fonts for the licensed real fonts
